The (In,Ga)As-(Ga,Mn)As core-shell nanowires exhibit ferromagnetic coupling and superparamagnetic behavior.
The Mn content in the (Ga,Mn)As shell is 5%.
The ferromagnetic coupling temperature threshold is 33 K.
The superparamagnetic behavior blocking temperature is 17 K.
The growth rate of the (In,Ga)As NWs is 1 µm/h.
The density of NWs is 2 x 10^9 NWs/cm^2.
The thickness of the (Ga,Mn)As layer deposited in-between the NWs is up to 70 nm.
The structural and chemical characterization method used is transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS).
The wurtzite structure confirmation method used is high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) and high-angle annular dark field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM).
The Raman scattering method used to estimate the carrier concentration in the NW shells is room temperature Raman scattering (RS) measurements.
The substrate temperature used to grow the (In,Ga)As cores is 500 °C.
The substrate temperature used to grow the (Ga,Mn)As shells is 220 °C.
The growth method used to fabricate the (In,Ga)As-(Ga,Mn)As core-shell nanowires is molecular beam epitaxy (MBE).

The (In,Ga)As-(Ga,Mn)As core-shell nanowires have a hexagonal cross-section.
The (Ga,Mn)As shell thickness is increasing slightly along the NW lengths.
The NWs have either hexagonal or round cross-sections depending on the shell thickness and spatial arrangement of nanowires.
The high-temperature grown (In,Ga)As NW cores have perfect hexagonal cross-sections.
The (Ga,Mn)As shells are epitaxial with respect to the (In,Ga)As cores without any dislocations at the interface.
The (Ga,Mn)As shells have a smooth surface without any misfit dislocations.
The (Ga,Mn)As shells have a Mn content of 5%.
The (Ga,Mn)As shells have a carrier concentration of 2 x 10^18 cm^-3.
